title: Authentication & Authorization
intro: Authentication and authorization are separate concerns that Rails interviews often conflate — and separating them clearly is itself an interview signal. Authentication is 'who are you?'; authorization is 'what can you do?'. Devise handles authentication for session-based Rails apps and can be extended with devise-jwt for token APIs. Doorkeeper turns a Rails app into an OAuth 2.0 provider. Pundit models authorization as plain Ruby policy objects — one class per resource, one method per action, easy to test without loading Rails. CanCanCan uses a single Ability class and is older but still common. This page covers all four plus JWT security (the algorithm confusion attack, why you always specify the algorithm explicitly), and the session vs token trade-off for Rails APIs.
